rationale: Evidence from van Oirsouw et al. (2025, 2026) and complementary cohorts confirms that KDM2B pathogenic variants show marked domain-dependent genotype-phenotype divergence. Specifically, variants clustered within the zinc-finger CxxC DNA-binding domain cause a distinct, highly penetrant syndromic presentation characterized by a distinct facial gestalt, high rates of congenital heart defects (up to 78%), ocular abnormalities, and urogenital/renal malformations. In contrast, aggregated cohort analysis of 68 individuals (47 with (likely) pathogenic variants) establishes that non-CxxC truncating loss-of-function and JmjC catalytic domain variants exhibit variable expressivity, incomplete penetrance, and significantly less extensive multisystem organ involvement, presenting predominantly with neurodevelopmental delay/intellectual disability without the full syndromic triad.

evidence.text: In an aggregated cohort of 68 individuals (evaluating 37 variants in 47 individuals classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic), analysis confirmed a highly penetrant CxxC-related phenotype with distinct facial features, contrasting sharply with the variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance observed for loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants.

source.title: Comprehensive Assessment of the KDM2B‐Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder and the 12q24. 31 Microdeletion Syndrome
source.quote: We analyzed genotype-phenotype correlations of this cohort combined with previously reported individuals (n = 68) and classify 37 variants in 47 individuals as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. We observe a highly penetrant CxxC-related phenotype with distinct facial features supported by GestaltMatcher. In contrast, our findings point to variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of loss-of-function variants and JmjC domain variants complicating variant classification and genetic counseling.

evidence.text: Characterization of 19 individuals with CxxC domain variants demonstrated that their core phenotype is significantly more extensive than that of individuals with KDM2B haploinsufficiency, exhibiting congenital heart defects in up to 78% of individuals alongside frequent ophthalmological and urogenital anomalies.

source.title: KDM2B variants in the CxxC domain impair its DNA-binding ability and cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: The core phenotype of the KDM2B-CxxC cohort is more extensive as compared to that of individuals with KDM2B haploinsufficiency. All individuals with CxxC variants presented with developmental delay, mainly in the speech and motor domain, in addition to variable intellectual disability and mild facial dysmorphism. Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals, with additional common findings including musculoskeletal, ophthalmological, and urogenital anomalies, as well as behavioral challenges and feeding difficulties.

evidence.text: Independent clinical reports confirm that missense variants localized to the CxxC zinc-finger DNA-binding domain consistently produce the syndromic multisystem triad, specifically ocular anomalies, congenital heart defects (e.g., ASD, VSD), and renal malformations (such as solitary kidney).

source.title: KDM2B‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder A Case‐Series Supporting the CxxC Domain Phenotype With Emphasis on Ocular and Dermatologic Features
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: Patient 1 is a 2-year-old boy with developmental delay, solitary kidney, atrial septal defect, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism... Patient 3 is a 5-year-old girl with autism, developmental delay, atrial septal defect, and ventricular septal defect, hypertrichosis, atopic dermatitis, and myopic astigmatism.

evidence.text: Targeted cohort screening of developmental eye anomaly cohorts identified CxxC domain variants that associate directly with severe structural eye malformations alongside cardiac and renal defects, confirming the CxxC domain as critical for the multisystem organ phenotype.

source.title: Variants in the CxxC domain of the epigenetic regulator KDM2B support its role in developmental eye anomalies
source.quote: By screening 706 families with developmental eye disorders, we identified two cases with KDM2B-CxxC variants... Both individuals exhibited complex structural eye defects, with neurodevelopmental, cardiac and renal anomalies variably present. These cases strengthen the association between KDM2B-CxxC variants and eye, kidney and heart malformations.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact organ-specific penetrance rates of cardiac, ocular, and urogenital malformations in strictly truncating LoF vs JmjC domain missense variants within the aggregated cohort?
new_directions.rationale: While van Oirsouw et al. established incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity for non-CxxC/JmjC variants compared to CxxC variants, reporting exact percentages for isolated LoF versus missense variants in the JmjC domain will refine diagnostic algorithms.

new_directions.question_text: Does the CxxC domain-specific episignature reliably differentiate pathogenic CxxC variants from benign or non-penetrant variants across unselected neurodevelopmental cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Because CxxC mutations confer a distinct subepisignature, determining its analytical specificity in patients presenting with isolated neurodevelopmental delay could establish methylation profiling as a first-line discriminator.
